name: 7. Large Language Models: GPT, Llama & Qwen

quiz.question: What is the primary training objective of a GPT-style base language model?
options: Next-token prediction using causal autoregressive context
quiz.explanation: GPT-style base language models are trained on the causal language modeling objective: maximizing the log-likelihood of predicting the true next token given all prior tokens.

quiz.question: Which neural architecture is standard for modern generative foundation models (GPT, Llama, Qwen)?
options: Recurrent Neural Network with Highway Connections
quiz.explanation: Modern generative language models use decoder-only Transformers because all language generation tasks can be formulated as next-token prediction without requiring a separate bidirectional encoder.

quiz.question: What is the primary function of a tokenizer in an LLM pipeline?
options: Update neural network weight matrices during backpropagation
Convert natural language text strings into discrete numerical token IDs
quiz.explanation: Neural networks process numerical tensors. A tokenizer decomposes raw text into discrete subwords or bytes and maps them to integer vocabulary IDs.

quiz.question: What mechanism prevents a decoder position from accessing future tokens during training?
quiz.explanation: A causal mask sets attention scores for all future positions (j > i) to negative infinity (-inf), ensuring Softmax assigns exactly 0.0 probability to future tokens.

quiz.question: What happens during LLM pretraining?
options: The model learns patterns, grammar, and reasoning from a large training corpus
Weights are randomly deleted to compress storage
The tokenizer is replaced on every request
quiz.explanation: Pretraining is self-supervised training on trillions of tokens where the model learns linguistic structure, factual knowledge, and reasoning capabilities.

quiz.question: What is a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture?
options: A network with no Transformer blocks
A system that dynamically routes tokens through selected expert networks
quiz.explanation: An MoE model contains multiple feed-forward expert networks per block; a learned parametric router selects only top-k experts per token, decoupling total parameters from active compute.

quiz.question: What does a context window define?
options: The applicable token budget for a sequence or request
quiz.explanation: The context window specifies the maximum number of tokens that the model can process concurrently in a single forward pass, shared across system prompt, history, query, and output.

quiz.question: What is the primary purpose of Key-Value (KV) caching during autoregressive decoding?
options: Store user login credentials in secure storage
Reuse earlier Key and Value representations during decoding to avoid redundant recalculation
quiz.explanation: Autoregressive generation generates one token at a time. KV caching stores earlier Key and Value representations in GPU memory, reducing per-token decoding complexity from O(T) to O(1).

quiz.question: What does top-p (nucleus) sampling control?
options: The cumulative probability mass threshold of eligible candidate tokens
quiz.explanation: Top-p sampling dynamically selects the smallest set of candidate tokens whose cumulative Softmax probability mass equals or exceeds threshold p.

quiz.question: What is the main purpose of model quantization (e.g. FP16 -> INT4)?
options: Reduce numerical representation precision and potentially memory requirements
quiz.explanation: Quantization represents weights with lower bit-widths (e.g. 4 bits instead of 16 bits), slashing model VRAM requirements by up to 4x and speeding up memory-bound inference.
